page: Microsoft Azure E8d_v4 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine from the EDv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Additionally, the instance is equipped with 307 GB of local storage, though it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals average performance across several compute and memory metrics, alongside specific bottlenecks. The Intel Xeon processor delivers average single-core and multi-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, supported by an L3 cache of 35 MB and AVX-512 instruction sets. While cached memory bandwidth for small blocks is average at 413.99 GB/sec, large-block uncached read and write memory bandwidth falls into the bottom 25% tier. Similarly, single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression are weak, though multi-threaded bzip3 decompression scales to average levels.

The E8d_v4 is configured for memory-intensive workloads that benefit from local scratch storage, such as relational databases, caching layers, and medium-scale data processing. Passmark database operations and Redis SET benchmarks demonstrate average throughput, with Redis achieving 6.53 million operations per second. However, the server exhibits poor performance in medium-parameter LLM inference and weak static web serving throughput, indicating it is less suited for intensive AI generation or high-volume web hosting. The qualitative cost profile reflects a high-density memory allocation paired with local storage, offering a balanced resource tradeoff for database hosting without the premium of GPU accelerators.
